parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no facility/bathroom restriction (index says bathroom access protected), no documented border or document friction for foreign travellers, no police targeting or custody-placement rule in the record, and gender identity is covered in employment/housing/healthcare anti-discrimination law as interpreted. The one trans-specific killing (2022 bar murder, 34 stab wounds) drew a 12-year sentence with the provocation defence rejected — a single incident with a strongly protective state response, which per the rubric is weak evidence of rate and positive evidence of institutions. The countervailing signals are social rather than institutional: LGBTIQ respondents avoid locations at 40% vs 29% regional and rank first of 30 for hiding at work, and no gender-identity hate-crime provision exists — a climate/recourse gap, not a traveller-facing ban. This is the 0.75 tier: acceptance and functioning courts, limited friction, uneven remedy documentation, not the broad audited visitor protection of 0.85.
